description:
Ditching simulations to hunt raw, punishing terrain.

Hunting the coldest, driest extremes to ensure our gear survives the actual frontier.
summary:
Earth cannot replicate the Moon or Mars. Outdoor terrestrial sites cannot copy 1/6 g or 3/8 g gravity, vacuum, thin carbon-dioxide air, cosmic radiation, or sub-110 K cryogenic cold traps. They can provide rigorous operational rehearsals for specific engineering challenges if matched with open satellite measurements.

We developed Partial Match, an open-source screening pipeline that evaluated 577,134 global 0.2-degree land cells against two exploration targets: the Artemis south-polar ridge (Nobile Rim 1 / Shackleton Ridge) and Martian shallow ground-ice plains (Arcadia Planitia). Rather than hunting for scenic look-alikes, our model scores measurable operational traits: 30 m geomorphic slope gradients from Copernicus DEM, nighttime land surface cooling from Terra MODIS, regolith barrenness from MODIS NDVI, and hyper-aridity from GPM IMERG.

The pipeline identified the Western Kunlun / Aksai Chin high plateau (36.1° N, 78.3° E) as Earth's top barren cold-desert analog cluster outside textbook deserts, scoring alongside our Atacama benchmark control. A public single-page web dashboard maps every candidate, isolates data-backed similarities, states physical failure boundaries, and details concrete field tests for rover climbs and permafrost drilling
details:
What it does and how it works

Partial Match replaces subjective visual analog selection with an open-source data pipeline. It evaluates 577,134 land cells globally (0.2° × 0.2° grid) against locked exploration targets:

  1. Lunar South Pole Base: Nobile Rim 1 / Shackleton Ridge, targeting 5°–15° rover mobility slopes, sunlit high-ground illumination, and adjacent cryogenic shadow boundaries.
  2. Martian Mid-Latitude Base: Arcadia Planitia (AP-1 / Badger Crater), targeting flat plains (<5° slope) overlying 0.1–2 m shallow subsurface water ice.

The pipeline extracts multi-sensor satellite data from NASA Earthdata and ESA Copernicus:

  • Terra MODIS MOD11C3 v061: Monthly 0.05° nighttime Land Surface Temperature to isolate sub-freezing permafrost ground.
  • Terra MODIS MOD13C2 v061: Monthly NDVI filtered to 0.005–0.060 to isolate barren rock regolith while excluding snow, surface water, and vegetative root networks.
  • GPM IMERG Final v07: Monthly precipitation rate (<0.01 mm/hr) to identify hyper-arid rain shadows that preserve dry regolith mechanics.
  • Copernicus DEM GLO-30: 30 m elevation and geomorphic slope to verify atmospheric thinning (>4,800 m a.s.l., ~520 hPa) and local terrain slope bands.

Factors considered

  • Elevation: High altitude cuts atmospheric column density, replicating high solar UV irradiance and radiative heat loss.
  • Geomorphic slope: Lander safety requires slopes under 5° to 8°, while resource-prospecting rovers require 5° to 15° climbs.
  • Thermal extremes: Sub-freezing night temperatures preserve subsurface ice and stress rover battery heaters.
  • Surface barrenness: Drills and tracks need unconsolidated clasts and periglacial till without biological root stabilization.
  • Moisture suppression: Hyper-aridity prevents chemical weathering and soil cohesion.

Project creativity and design discipline

Visual analog selection fails because a landscape that looks like Mars on camera can have wet soil, warm night air, thick atmospheric drag, or dense root systems. Partial Match enforces three non-negotiable boundaries:

  1. Every candidate has three mandatory sections: Matches, Breaks, and Mission Rehearsals.
  2. Earth physics boundaries are explicitly stated: Earth cannot replicate 1/6 g or 3/8 g gravity, vacuum, 6 mbar carbon-dioxide air, galactic cosmic radiation, or permanently shadowed lunar cold traps (<110 K).
  3. Every discovery candidate (Site A: Western Kunlun / Aksai Chin, 36.1° N, 78.3° E) is scored against a famous benchmark control (Site B: Atacama Desert, Chile) with the identical mathematical formula.

Tools, software, and data

  • Languages and libraries: Python 3.11, Pandas, NumPy, Rasterio, Leaflet, MapLibre GL.
  • Data sources: NASA Earthdata CMR API, Terra MODIS, GPM IMERG, ESA Copernicus DEM GLO-30, NASA PDS LRO LOLA 5 mpp, NASA PDS Diviner, MGS MOLA.
  • Deliverables: Single-page desktop mission dashboard with zero internal scroll (web/index.html), reproducible scoring script (screen.py), verified data provenance log (sources.csv), detailed scientific dossiers (RESULTS.html), and a 7-slide presentation (slides.html).

Intended impact

This pipeline equips space agencies and rover engineers with an empirical roadmap for field trials. Instead of claiming a single location simulates an entire planet, teams can deploy rovers to Western Kunlun specifically to rehearse 8°–15° moraine navigation and rotary permafrost drilling, while reserving the Atacama for dry evaporite mechanics, knowing the quantitative limits of both.
